messages.subject: Questions on cross-lagged panel model
parts:
I have five questions on cross lagged panel model.

Q1: do we proceed with two-step procedure? First is CFA. Second is SEM. I don't think so because the 2 should give us the same results. 

Q2: With cross-lagged, we can go for either correlated residual or uncorrelated residual. Conceptually, are there any differences?

Q3: I downloaded some Lavaan examples from Dr. Newsom's website (http://www.longitudinalsem.com/).. Why should we repeat the variable "w1happy "  and use "NA" at first？ The first loading is already set to 1 by default

model5.2c <- '  #common labels for loadings imposes longitudinal equality constraints;
#referent identification--first loading is referent by default;

     w1posaff =~ NA*w1happy + (lambda1)*w1happy + (lambda2)*w1enjoy + (lambda3)*w1satis + (lambda4)*w1joyful + (lambda5)*w1please
     w2posaff =~ NA*w2happy + (lambda1)*w2happy + (lambda2)*w2enjoy + (lambda3)*w2satis + (lambda4)*w2joyful + (lambda5)*w2please
     w1unw =~ NA*w1unw1 + (lambda6)*w1unw1 + (lambda7)*w1unw2 + (lambda8)*w1unw3
     w2unw =~ NA*w2unw1 + (lambda6)*w2unw1 + (lambda7)*w2unw2 + (lambda8)*w2unw3

#set exogenous factor variance for first occasion identificaiton;. 
w1posaff ~~ 1*w1posaff
w1unw ~~ 1*w1unw

#cross-lagged and autoregressive effects;
w2posaff ~ w1posaff + w1unw
    w2unw ~ w1unw + w1posaff 

#correlated measurement residuals;
w1happy ~~ w2happy
w1enjoy ~~ w2enjoy
w1satis ~~ w2satis
w1joyful ~~ w2joyful
w1please ~~ w2please
    w1unw1 ~~ w2unw1
w1unw2 ~~ w2unw2
w1unw3 ~~ w2unw3 '

fitmodel5.2c <- sem(model5.2c, data=socex1.1, information="expected")
summary(fitmodel5.2c, fit.measures=TRUE, standardized=TRUE, rsquare=TRUE)

Q4: The question is also related the example from the above website. Apart from repeating the variable at first and use "NA" at front, Lamda1 is obtained via an equation. I understand the repetition and use of equation is for identification purposes. Can anyone be more specific?

model5.2a <- ' #common labels for loadings imposes longitudinal equality constraints;

     w1posaff =~ NA*w1happy + (lambda1)*w1happy + (lambda2)*w1enjoy + (lambda3)*w1satis + (lambda4)*w1joyful + (lambda5)*w1please
     w2posaff =~ NA*w2happy + (lambda1)*w2happy + (lambda2)*w2enjoy + (lambda3)*w2satis + (lambda4)*w2joyful + (lambda5)*w2please
     w1unw =~ NA*w1unw1 + (lambda6)*w1unw1 + (lambda7)*w1unw2 + (lambda8)*w1unw3
     w2unw =~ NA*w2unw1 + (lambda6)*w2unw1 + (lambda7)*w2unw2 + (lambda8)*w2unw3

#cross-lagged and autoregressive effects;  
w2posaff ~ w1posaff + w1unw
    w2unw ~ w1unw + w1posaff 

#correlated measurement residuals;
w1happy ~~ w2happy
w1enjoy ~~ w2enjoy
w1satis ~~ w2satis
w1joyful ~~ w2joyful
w1please ~~ w2please
    w1unw1 ~~ w2unw1
w1unw2 ~~ w2unw2
w1unw3 ~~ w2unw3
#complex constraints for effects coding identification;

lambda1 == 5 - lambda2 - lambda3 - lambda4 - lambda5
lambda6 == 3 - lambda7 - lambda8  '

fitmodel5.2a <- sem(model5.2a, data=socex1.1, information="expected")
summary(fitmodel5.2a, fit.measures=TRUE, standardized=TRUE, rsquare=TRUE)

Q5. WIth my dataset, I followed Dr. Newsom's example, using different ways (correlated or uncorrelated residual, NA and repetition of first variable, equation, etc. I got the following warning message from Lavaan. Is the result valid? The data is ordinal and I used WLSMV. 

In muthen1984(Data = X[[g]], ov.names = ov.names[[g]], ov.types = ov.types,  :
  lavaan WARNING: trouble constructing W matrix; used generalized inverse for A11 submatrix 

Would appreciate if anyone can help.

Melissa

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Questions on cross-lagged panel model
parts: Q1: do we proceed with two-step procedure? First is CFA. Second is SEM. I don't think so because the 2 should give us the same results.

If your latent structure is saturated, then df between CFA and SEM will be equivalent, and the models will be statistically equivalent.  But CFA could still be useful for testing invariance of measurement parameters across occasions before drawing inferences about effects over time.
Q2: With cross-lagged, we can go for either correlated residual or uncorrelated residual. Conceptually, are there any differences?

Yes, correlated residuals between the same item over time represent the theory that the same item-specific (but not common-factor) component of the indicator affects it over time, and those effects over time are correlated for the same reason you allow common factors to correlated with themselves over time.

Q3: I downloaded some lavaan examples from Dr. Newsom's website (http://www.longitudinalsem.com/).. Why should we repeat the variable "w1happy "  and use "NA" at first？ The first loading is already set to 1 by default
w1posaff =~ NA*w1happy + (lambda1)*w1happy

That is only necessary to do 2 things to the same parameter: freely estimate it (NA*w1happy) and give that estimate a label (lambda1*w1happy), which makes it easier to apply equality constraints by specifying the same label for multiple parameters.

The freeing part would not be necessary if you identified the model by standardizing the latent variable (std.lv = TRUE) instead of fixing a loading to 1.  But this example identifies the model by neither of those typical methods, but instead uses the effects-coding method (Little et al., 2006), which are the constraints specified at the bottom of the syntax.  You can read about that method here:

http://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1207/s15328007sem1301_3

Q4: The question is also related the example from the above website. Apart from repeating the variable at first and use "NA" at front, Lamda1 is obtained via an equation. I understand the repetition and use of equation is for identification purposes. Can anyone be more specific?

Did I already answer your question above?  Also read this for more information:

http://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/syntax2.html

Q5. WIth my dataset, I followed Dr. Newsom's example, using different ways (correlated or uncorrelated residual, NA and repetition of first variable, equation, etc. I got the following warning message from Lavaan. Is the result valid? The data is ordinal and I used WLSMV.

Need more information to know what the problem is.  Please provide syntax and output.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
UvA web page: http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

parts:
Thank you for your help, Terry. Really appreciate that.

  I attached the file at the end. For this syntax, I have also tried other typical methods--equality constraints, etc. All produced the same error message;

  Error in if (combined.weights & probably.not.combined.weights) warning(paste("Data do not look like combined weights: mean replication weight is",  : 
  missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed.

  If I set combined.weights=F (you know this is not true), an opposite warning occurred.

  Error in if (!combined.weights & probably.combined.weights) warning(paste("Data look like combined weights: mean replication weight is",  : 
  missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed.

   I thought about different reasons for the warning, such as contaminated file , syntax error, computer virus. To fix the potential issues, I downloaded the dataset, scanned the computer for virus, updated R program and tried the code at different computers. Still the warning. While trying to solve the problem, I found another interesting message with another dataset.

In muthen1984(Data = X[[g]], ov.names = ov.names[[g]], ov.types = ov.types,  :
  lavaan WARNING: trouble constructing W matrix; used generalized inverse for A11 submatrix

I didn't get any warning message with the same R syntax to analyze the same dataset in the past. Everything was fine in the past. The only difference is R version. 

   Would greatly appreciate if you can help.

Melissa. 
  .
